Your job in this session is to invent 7 new alpha factor(s)
that complement an existing seed ensemble.

DATA CONTEXT
------------
You are working with the configured market-data feed (10-second bars).  When you write a factor, the ``data``
dict passed to ``calc`` exposes the fields below as ``pd.DataFrame``
(index = bar timestamps, columns = tickers).  Every field below is
available — pick whichever ones your idea actually needs; do NOT use any
field that is not listed (the factor would be rejected as out-of-scope).

Price / OHLCV view:

    open      : start-of-bar price (mid-price on LOBSTER)
    high      : intra-bar high (max(mid, midEnd) on LOBSTER)
    low       : intra-bar low (min(mid, midEnd) on LOBSTER)
    close     : end-of-bar price (mid-price on LOBSTER)
    volume    : traded volume in the bar (|signed trade| on LOBSTER)

Notes:
- All fields are aligned on the same DatetimeIndex and the same ticker
  columns, so cross-field arithmetic is safe.
- Do NOT pass extra keyword arguments to the helper operators below —
  they take positional arguments only.

Fundamental / estimate / event fields (point-in-time, quarterly):

    sector    : GICS-style sector label (text, e.g. "Technology"). Static.
    industry  : finer industry label (text). Static.
    marketCap : market capitalization in USD (daily where the feed
                supplies it, otherwise per fiscal quarter).
    peRatio   : price / earnings (float; negative for loss-makers).
    pbRatio   : price / book.
    psRatio   : price / sales.
    roe       : return on equity.
    roic      : return on invested capital.
    debtToEquity : leverage ratio.
    currentRatio : liquidity ratio.
    grossMargin : gross profitability margin (fraction).
    netMargin   : net profitability margin (fraction).
    revenue   : quarterly revenue (USD).
    eps       : reported EPS (USD).
    freeCashFlow : free cash flow in USD (operating cash flow − capex).
    epsEstimate    : analyst EPS consensus for the latest quarter.
    revenueEstimate: analyst revenue consensus for the latest quarter.
    epsSurprise : reported EPS − estimate (post-earnings-drift signal).
    enterpriseValue          : market cap + debt − cash.
    costOfRevenue            : cost of goods sold.
    grossProfit              : revenue − COGS.
    rdExpense                : R&D spend.
    sgaExpense               : SG&A spend.
    operatingExpenses        : total operating expenses.
    ebitda                   : earnings before interest, tax, D&A.
    ebit                     : earnings before interest and tax.
    operatingIncome          : operating profit.
    interestExpense          : interest paid on debt.
    incomeBeforeTax          : pre-tax profit.
    incomeTaxExpense         : tax charge.
    netIncome                : bottom-line profit.
    epsDiluted               : diluted EPS.
    sharesOutstanding        : weighted average shares outstanding — the point-in-time share count.
    sharesDiluted            : diluted share count.
    depreciationAmortization : D&A charge.
    cash                     : cash and equivalents.
    receivables              : net receivables.
    inventory                : inventory.
    totalCurrentAssets       : current assets.
    ppe                      : net property, plant & equipment.
    goodwill                 : goodwill.
    intangibleAssets         : intangibles ex-goodwill.
    totalAssets              : total assets.
    accountsPayable          : payables.
    shortTermDebt            : debt due within a year.
    totalCurrentLiabilities  : current liabilities.
    longTermDebt             : long-term debt.
    totalLiabilities         : total liabilities.
    totalDebt                : short + long-term debt.
    totalEquity              : book equity.
    retainedEarnings         : cumulative retained profit.
    operatingCashFlow        : cash from operations.
    capex                    : capital expenditure (negative).
    stockBasedCompensation   : SBC charge.

    acquisitionsNet          : cash spent on acquisitions.

    pfcfRatio                : price / free cash flow.
    pocfRatio                : price / operating cash flow.
    earningsYield            : earnings / price — the PE inverse.
    freeCashFlowYield        : FCF / market cap.
    dividendYield            : dividend / price.

    evToEbitda               : enterprise value / EBITDA.
    evToOperatingCashFlow    : EV / operating cash flow.
    evToFreeCashFlow         : EV / free cash flow.

    debtToCapital            : debt / (debt + equity).
    financialLeverage        : assets / equity.
    interestCoverage         : EBIT / interest expense.
    netDebtToEbitda          : net debt / EBITDA.
    quickRatio               : liquid assets / current liabilities.
    cashRatio                : cash / current liabilities.
    workingCapital           : current assets − current liabilities.
    investedCapital          : capital employed in the business.
    assetTurnover            : revenue / assets.
    receivablesTurnover      : revenue / receivables.
    payablesTurnover         : COGS / payables.
    inventoryTurnover        : COGS / inventory.
    daysSalesOutstanding     : receivable days.
    daysPayablesOutstanding  : payable days.
    daysInventoryOutstanding : inventory days.
    cashConversionCycle      : DSO + DIO − DPO.
    operatingCycle           : DSO + DIO.
    revenuePerShare          : revenue / shares.
    netIncomePerShare        : earnings / shares.
    bookValuePerShare        : book equity / shares.
    tangibleBookValuePerShare: tangible book / shares.
    cashPerShare             : cash / shares.
    operatingCashFlowPerShare: OCF / shares.
    freeCashFlowPerShare     : FCF / shares.
    capexPerShare            : capex / shares.
    revenueGrowth            : revenue growth.
    grossProfitGrowth        : gross profit growth.
    ebitGrowth               : EBIT growth.
    ebitdaGrowth             : EBITDA growth.
    operatingIncomeGrowth    : operating income growth.
    netIncomeGrowth          : net income growth.
    epsGrowth                : EPS growth.
    epsDilutedGrowth         : diluted EPS growth.
    sharesGrowth             : share-count growth — negative means buybacks.
    dividendPerShareGrowth   : DPS growth.
    operatingCashFlowGrowth  : OCF growth.
    freeCashFlowGrowth       : FCF growth.
    assetGrowth              : total-asset growth — the classic asset-growth anomaly.
    debtGrowth               : debt growth.
    bookValuePerShareGrowth  : BVPS growth.
    receivablesGrowth        : receivables growth.
    inventoryGrowth          : inventory growth.
    rdExpenseGrowth          : R&D growth.
    sgaExpenseGrowth         : SG&A growth.
    revenueGrowth3Y          : 3-year revenue/share growth.
    revenueGrowth5Y          : 5-year revenue/share growth.
    netIncomeGrowth3Y        : 3-year earnings/share growth.
    netIncomeGrowth5Y        : 5-year earnings/share growth.
    epsActual                : reported EPS at the release.
    revenueActual            : reported revenue at the release.
    revenueSurprise          : reported revenue − estimate (derived).

LOOK-AHEAD — read carefully.  These fields are **already point-in-time**:
each value is stamped at its *availability date* (the filing / report date,
or fiscal-period-end + a reporting lag) and forward-filled, so reading
``data["peRatio"]`` at date t only ever sees what was public by t.  You do
NOT need to (and must not) shift them yourself.  They are **quarterly step
functions**: ``NaN`` before a name's first report and after a long staleness
gap, and otherwise constant between reports — so be defensive (``.fillna``,
``df.where(...)``) and prefer cross-sectional ops (``rank``) and slow changes
(quarter-over-quarter ``delta``) over fast time-series ops.

PREDICTION HORIZON
------------------
This run uses ONE fixed forecast horizon for every factor: ``prediction_horizon = 6`` bars (each bar spans **10 second** of wall-clock time; so this run is fixed at ~6 10-second bars ahead).
Do not choose a separate horizon for the idea.  Every brainstormed idea and every generated factor class must declare exactly ``prediction_horizon = 6``; set ``suggested_horizons`` to ``[6]`` or omit it.  Valid range: 1 ≤ prediction_horizon ≤ 2000 bars.


INPUT PAPERS
------------
You have been given the following research papers to draw inspiration
from.  Use them critically — paraphrase or build on the ideas, do not
copy formulas blindly.  You are also free to lean on your own beliefs
about how markets work, as long as the resulting factor is grounded
in the data we actually have.

(no papers loaded for this session — rely on your own knowledge)

PAPER-TO-FACTOR STANDARD
------------------------
Read the paper like a researcher implementing a mechanism, not like a prompt
asking for a familiar formula.  Extract the paper's actual object of interest
(state variable, event process, path shape, residual, tail behaviour, regime,
or interaction), map it to the fields available here, and implement the closest
causal approximation.  You are NOT confined to a fixed operator vocabulary: if
a paper turns on truncated path signatures, Hawkes-process intensities,
spectral / wavelet / entropy features, rolling eigen-structure, or any other
richer transform, propose exactly that — the codegen step implements such maths
directly as vectorised, causal numpy/scipy code, so do not pre-emptively flatten
it into a rank/mean/delta.  Creative, method-faithful mechanisms are precisely
what this stage is for, as long as they remain computable from the listed
fields and leak-free.

NOVELTY & MECHANISM BAR
-----------------------
Propose ideas a discerning quant PM would respect — not the millionth 20-day
momentum or moving-average-crossover variant.  Avoid the over-mined families
(plain momentum, simple short-horizon reversal, textbook volatility / value
ranks) unless you add a genuinely new conditioning variable, interaction, or
transform.  Make each mechanism precise enough to be falsifiable: what
observation would kill it, who is on the other side of the trade, and why the
inefficiency persists (limits to arbitrage, structural or mandate constraints,
behavioural bias, slow-moving capital).  Prefer under-explored relationships
BETWEEN the listed fields over yet another transform of ``close`` alone.

WHAT TO PRODUCE
---------------
Propose exactly 7 distinct factor ideas.  Each idea must:

  - have a unique snake_case `factor_id` (lowercase, ascii, starting
    with a letter, ≤ 60 chars) that does NOT collide with any of the
    existing factor IDs below;
  - belong to one of the categories: momentum, mean_reversion,
    volatility, microstructure, statistical_arbitrage, carry, sentiment,
    or other;
  - state a clear `trading_idea` — the *why*, in 2-4 sentences.  The
    mechanism may be economic OR mathematical / statistical /
    microstructural / behavioural — reasoning like "Hawkes-process
    self-excitation describes clustering of order flow" is as valid as
    a market-structure or behavioural-finance story, as long as it is
    grounded and falsifiable; cite the source paper(s) if relevant;
  - declare a `prediction_horizon` (positive integer number of bars) —
    the forward offset at which the signal's edge is expected to
    materialise (see the PREDICTION HORIZON note in the DATA CONTEXT);
    optionally a few `suggested_horizons` worth measuring;
  - be cross-sectional (return a DataFrame indexed by time, columns =
    tickers, like the seed alphas);
  - be computable from the fields listed in the DATA CONTEXT above;
  - be diverse — no two ideas may be minor variations of one signal, and
    do not merely rename a standard rolling mean/rank/correlation as a
    sophisticated paper concept.

    """Amihud illiquidity shock: a spike in price impact demands a premium.

    Mechanism: when a name's price impact per dollar traded jumps relative to

    subsequent returns are higher until impact normalises (Amihud 2002)."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, ts_mean
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    @register_factor
    class AmihudShock(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "amihud_shock"
        name = "Amihud illiquidity shock"
        category = "microstructure"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of short-run Amihud price impact "
            "(5-bar mean of |return| per unit dollar volume) relative to its "
            "own 60-bar level: long names whose impact just spiked."
        )
        window_length = 60
        inputs = ["close", "volume"]
        prediction_horizon = 6      # bars over which the liquidity premium accrues
        suggested_horizons = [3, 6, 12]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            close = data["close"]
            ret = returns(data)
            dollar = (close * data["volume"]).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            illiq = ret.abs() / dollar            # Amihud (2002) price impact
            base = ts_mean(illiq, 60).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            return rank(ts_mean(illiq, 5) / base)

written as a small vectorised, causal helper.  This is what "implement the

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (

        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:

            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:

        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:

        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (

        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, delta, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class DebtToEquityTrend(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "debt_to_equity_trend"
    name = "Debt to Equity Trend"
    category = "value"
    description = (
        "This signal calculates the trend in the debt-to-equity ratio over recent quarters, highlighting companies that are successfully deleveraging."
    )
    inputs = ["debtToEquity"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        debt_to_equity = data["debtToEquity"].fillna(0.0)
        trend = delta(debt_to_equity, 1)  # Calculate the change in debt-to-equity ratio
        trend_mean = ts_mean(trend, 4)  # Calculate the mean trend over the last 4 quarters
        return rank(trend_mean)  # Rank the trend values"
}

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:

        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

This factor aims to capture these events, as they often precede significant price movements. The idea is grounded in the belief that sudden spikes in activity can indicate shifts in market sentiment and potential reversals."""

```python
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, ts_max, ts_min, adv, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class PriceVolumeSurge(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "price_volume_surge"
    name = "Price-Volume Surge"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "This signal identifies instances where price increases significantly while volume exceeds its historical average, "
        "signaling potential momentum or reversal opportunities."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # Calculate the average volume over the last 60 bars
        avg_volume = adv(volume, 60)

        # Calculate the price surge as the difference from the previous close
        price_surge = close - close.shift(1)

        # Identify significant price increases where the current volume exceeds the historical average
        surge_condition = (price_surge > 0) & (volume > avg_volume)

        # Calculate the rank of the price surge condition
        surge_rank = rank(surge_condition.astype(float))

        return surge_rank.fillna(0.0)
```

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (

        prediction_horizon = 12

This factor aims to capture these events, as they often precede significant price movements. The idea is grounded in the belief that sudden spikes in activity can indicate shifts in market sentiment and potential reversals."""

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, ts_max, ts_min, adv, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class PriceVolumeSurge(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "price_volume_surge"
    name = "Price-Volume Surge"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "This signal identifies instances where price increases significantly while volume exceeds its historical average, "
        "signaling potential momentum or reversal opportunities."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # Calculate the average volume over the last 60 bars
        avg_volume = adv(volume, 60)

        # Calculate the price surge as the difference from the previous close
        price_surge = close - close.shift(1)

        # Identify significant price increases where the current volume exceeds the historical average
        surge_condition = (price_surge > 0) & (volume > avg_volume)

        # Calculate the rank of the price surge condition
        surge_rank = rank(surge_condition.astype(float))

        return surge_rank.fillna(0.0)
```

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

    """Amihud illiquidity shock: a spike in price impact demands a premium.

    Mechanism: when a name's price impact per dollar traded jumps relative to
    its own recent norm, liquidity providers demand compensation to hold it —
    subsequent returns are higher until impact normalises (Amihud 2002)."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, ts_mean
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    @register_factor
    class AmihudShock(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "amihud_shock"
        name = "Amihud illiquidity shock"
        category = "microstructure"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of short-run Amihud price impact "
            "(5-bar mean of |return| per unit dollar volume) relative to its "
            "own 60-bar level: long names whose impact just spiked."
        )
        window_length = 60
        inputs = ["close", "volume"]
        prediction_horizon = 6      # bars over which the liquidity premium accrues
        suggested_horizons = [3, 6, 12]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            close = data["close"]
            ret = returns(data)
            dollar = (close * data["volume"]).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            illiq = ret.abs() / dollar            # Amihud (2002) price impact
            base = ts_mean(illiq, 60).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            return rank(ts_mean(illiq, 5) / base)

Here the mechanism is NOT in ``ops`` — it is a Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio,
written as a small vectorised, causal helper.  This is what "implement the
paper's actual mechanism" looks like: plain numpy/pandas, trailing-only,

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
"""Stocks that exhibit high momentum tend to have lower volatility, as they are seen as stable trends. This factor exploits the relationship between momentum and volatility, identifying stocks that are showing strong upward price trends while maintaining lower-than-average volatility. This approach is based on the assumption that stability in price trends can lead to continued performance."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, stddev
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _momentum_volatility_correlation(momentum: pd.DataFrame, volatility: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Calculate the correlation between momentum and volatility."""
    return momentum.rolling(window=5).corr(volatility)


@register_factor
class MomentumVolatilityCorrelation(BaseFactor):
```
```python
    factor_id = "momentum_volatility_correlation"
    name = "Momentum-Volatility Correlation"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "This signal calculates the correlation between recent momentum (price return) and volatility (standard deviation of returns), "
        "highlighting stocks that show a strong positive momentum with low volatility."
    )
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        momentum = returns(data)
        volatility = stddev(momentum, 5).fillna(0.0)  # 5-bar rolling stddev
        correlation = _momentum_volatility_correlation(momentum, volatility)
        return rank(correlation)
```

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor  
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, stddev  
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor  

@register_factor  
class MomentumStabilityIndicator(BaseFactor):  
    factor_id = "momentum_stability_indicator"  
    name = "Momentum Stability Indicator"  
    category = "momentum"  
    description = (  
        "This signal ranks stocks based on their recent momentum (price return) and volatility (standard deviation of returns), "  
        "highlighting stocks with high momentum and low volatility that are likely to maintain their upward trends."  
    )  
    inputs = ["close"]  
    prediction_horizon = 6  
    suggested_horizons = [6]  
    expected_sign = 1  

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:  
        close = data["close"]  
        momentum = returns(data)  
        volatility = stddev(momentum, 5).fillna(0.0)  
        score = momentum / (volatility + 1e-8)  
        return rank(score)"

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
"""Market reactions to news and events often lead to overreactions, creating opportunities for mean reversion in prices. By analyzing the relationship between price movements and relative trading volumes during significant price changes, we can identify stocks that are likely to revert back to their mean price after a period of excessive sentiment, either bullish or bearish."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_sum, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class MarketSentimentReversion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "market_sentiment_reversion"
    name = "Market Sentiment Reversion"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "This factor computes the deviation of a stock's price from its recent mean, "
        "adjusted for the volume of trades during significant price spikes. A higher volume "
        "with a large price change suggests a crowded trade that is likely to revert."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].fillna(0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        ret = returns(data)

        # Calculate the mean price over the last 20 bars
        mean_price = ts_mean(close, 20)

        # Calculate the price deviation from the mean
        price_deviation = close - mean_price

        # Calculate the volume during significant price changes (threshold can be adjusted)
        significant_volume = volume.where(ret.abs() > 0.02, 0.0)

        # Calculate the signal as the price deviation adjusted by the significant volume
        signal = price_deviation / (significant_volume + 1e-10)  # Adding a small constant to avoid division by zero

        return rank(signal)
```

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, returns

class SentimentMeanReversion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sentiment_mean_reversion"
    name = "Sentiment Mean Reversion"
    category = "mean_reversion"

        "This factor computes the normalized price deviation from the recent mean price, "
        "adjusted for the volume during significant price changes. A higher deviation with "
        "significant volume suggests a crowded trade likely to revert."

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:

        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:

            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)

```python
"""Sentiment mean reversion: overreactions to news create opportunities for price corrections. By analyzing price changes and relative trading volumes, we can identify potential reversals."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class SentimentMeanReversion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sentiment_mean_reversion"
    name = "Sentiment Mean Reversion"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "This factor computes the normalized price deviation from the recent mean price, "
        "adjusted for the volume during significant price changes. A higher deviation with "
        "significant volume suggests a crowded trade likely to revert."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].fillna(0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        ret = returns(data)

        # Calculate the mean price over the last 20 bars
        mean_price = ts_mean(close, 20)

        # Calculate the price deviation from the mean
        price_deviation = close - mean_price

        # Calculate the significant volume during price changes (threshold can be adjusted)
        significant_volume = volume.where(ret.abs() > 0.01, 0.0)  # Changed threshold to 1%

        # Calculate the signal as the normalized price deviation adjusted by the significant volume
        signal = price_deviation / (significant_volume + 1e-10)  # Adding a small constant to avoid division by zero

        return rank(signal)
```

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
"""Sentiment mean reversion: overreactions to news create opportunities for price corrections. By analyzing price changes and relative trading volumes, we can identify potential reversals."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class SentimentMeanReversion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sentiment_mean_reversion"
    name = "Sentiment Mean Reversion"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "This factor computes the normalized price deviation from the recent mean price, "
        "adjusted for the volume during significant price changes. A higher deviation with "
        "significant volume suggests a crowded trade likely to revert."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].fillna(0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        ret = returns(data)

        # Calculate the mean price over the last 20 bars
        mean_price = ts_mean(close, 20)

        # Calculate the price deviation from the mean
        price_deviation = close - mean_price

        # Calculate the significant volume during price changes (threshold can be adjusted)
        significant_volume = volume.where(ret.abs() > 0.01, 0.0)  # Changed threshold to 1%

        # Calculate the signal as the normalized price deviation adjusted by the significant volume
        signal = price_deviation / (significant_volume + 1e-10)  # Adding a small constant to avoid division by zero

        return rank(signal)
```

    from __future__ import annotations

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
    category = "microstructure"

        "measuring the divergence between price changes and volume changes over a recent window."
    )
```

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, delta, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

@register_factor
class VolumePriceConvergence(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "volume_price_convergence"
    name = "Volume-Price Convergence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "The signal computes the cross-sectional rank of instances where price changes are supported by corresponding changes in volume, "
        "indicating stronger market signals. It focuses on identifying trends where price and volume are converging, suggesting a higher likelihood of continuation."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    expected_sign = 1

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # Calculate the price change and average volume over the last 60 bars
        price_change = delta(close, 1)
        avg_volume = ts_mean(volume, 60)

        # Calculate the volume change relative to the average
        volume_change = volume - avg_volume

        # Identify convergence conditions
        convergence_condition = (price_change > 0) & (volume_change > 0) | (price_change < 0) & (volume_change < 0)

        # Calculate the rank of the convergence condition
        convergence_rank = rank(convergence_condition.astype(float))

        return convergence_rank.fillna(0.0)
```

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""

        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
def _momentum_volatility_correlation(momentum: pd.DataFrame, volatility: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
```

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, ts_mean
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    @register_factor
    class AmihudShock(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "amihud_shock"
        name = "Amihud illiquidity shock"
        category = "microstructure"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of short-run Amihud price impact "
            "(5-bar mean of |return| per unit dollar volume) relative to its "
            "own 60-bar level: long names whose impact just spiked."
        )
        window_length = 60
        inputs = ["close", "volume"]
        prediction_horizon = 6      # bars over which the liquidity premium accrues

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
class SentimentMeanReversion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sentiment_mean_reversion"

    category = "mean_reversion"
```

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, ts_mean
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    @register_factor
    class AmihudShock(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "amihud_shock"
        name = "Amihud illiquidity shock"
        category = "microstructure"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of short-run Amihud price impact "
            "(5-bar mean of |return| per unit dollar volume) relative to its "
            "own 60-bar level: long names whose impact just spiked."
        )
        window_length = 60
        inputs = ["close", "volume"]
        prediction_horizon = 6      # bars over which the liquidity premium accrues
        suggested_horizons = [3, 6, 12]

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
"""Market reactions to news and events often lead to overreactions, creating opportunities for mean reversion in prices. By analyzing the relationship between price movements and relative trading volumes during significant price changes, we can identify stocks that are likely to revert back to their mean price after a period of excessive sentiment, either bullish or bearish."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_sum, returns
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class MarketSentimentReversion(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "market_sentiment_reversion"
    name = "Market Sentiment Reversion"
    category = "mean_reversion"
    description = (
        "This factor computes the deviation of a stock's price from its recent mean, "
        "adjusted for the volume of trades during significant price spikes. A higher volume "
        "with a large price change suggests a crowded trade that is likely to revert."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].fillna(0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        ret = returns(data)

        # Calculate the mean price over the last 20 bars
        mean_price = ts_mean(close, 20)

        # Calculate the price deviation from the mean
        price_deviation = close - mean_price

        # Calculate the volume during significant price changes (threshold can be adjusted)
        significant_volume = volume.where(ret.abs() > 0.02, 0.0)

        # Calculate the signal as the price deviation adjusted by the significant volume
        signal = price_deviation / (significant_volume + 1e-10)  # Adding a small constant to avoid division by zero

        return rank(signal)
```

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:

        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, delta, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

@register_factor
class VolumePriceConvergence(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "volume_price_convergence"
    name = "Volume-Price Convergence"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "The signal computes the cross-sectional rank of instances where price changes are supported by corresponding changes in volume, "
        "indicating stronger market signals. It focuses on identifying trends where price and volume are converging, suggesting a higher likelihood of continuation."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]
    expected_sign = 1

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # Calculate the price change and average volume over the last 60 bars
        price_change = delta(close, 1)
        avg_volume = ts_mean(volume, 60)

        # Calculate the volume change relative to the average
        volume_change = volume - avg_volume

        # Identify convergence conditions
        convergence_condition = (price_change > 0) & (volume_change > 0) | (price_change < 0) & (volume_change < 0)

        # Calculate the rank of the convergence condition
        convergence_rank = rank(convergence_condition.astype(float))

        return convergence_rank.fillna(0.0)
```

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

```python
"""An unusual surge in price accompanied by high volume can signify strong buying interest or selling pressure. This factor aims to capture these events, as they often precede significant price movements. The idea is grounded in the belief that sudden spikes in activity can indicate shifts in market sentiment and potential reversals."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import ts_mean, ts_max, ts_min, adv, rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


@register_factor
class PriceVolumeSurge(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "price_volume_surge"
    name = "Price-Volume Surge"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "This signal identifies instances where price increases significantly while volume exceeds its historical average, "
        "signaling potential momentum or reversal opportunities."
    )
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6  # bars ahead the edge peaks
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        # Calculate the average volume over the last 60 bars
        avg_volume = adv(volume, 60)

        # Calculate the price surge as the difference from the previous close
        price_surge = close - close.shift(1)

        # Identify significant price increases where the current volume exceeds the historical average
        surge_condition = (price_surge > 0) & (volume > avg_volume)

        # Calculate the rank of the price surge condition
        surge_rank = rank(surge_condition.astype(float))

        return surge_rank.fillna(0.0)
```

    """Amihud illiquidity shock: a spike in price impact demands a premium.

    Mechanism: when a name's price impact per dollar traded jumps relative to
    its own recent norm, liquidity providers demand compensation to hold it —
    subsequent returns are higher until impact normalises (Amihud 2002)."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns, ts_mean
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    @register_factor
    class AmihudShock(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "amihud_shock"
        name = "Amihud illiquidity shock"
        category = "microstructure"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of short-run Amihud price impact "
            "(5-bar mean of |return| per unit dollar volume) relative to its "
            "own 60-bar level: long names whose impact just spiked."
        )
        window_length = 60
        inputs = ["close", "volume"]
        prediction_horizon = 6      # bars over which the liquidity premium accrues
        suggested_horizons = [3, 6, 12]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            close = data["close"]
            ret = returns(data)
            dollar = (close * data["volume"]).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            illiq = ret.abs() / dollar            # Amihud (2002) price impact
            base = ts_mean(illiq, 60).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            return rank(ts_mean(illiq, 5) / base)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)
